1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% to align with observed mean reversion.

2. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% of 30d history), model tends to overshoot and stay elevated — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x the immediate prior value to avoid overreaction.

3. Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day for the last 5–10 days to reflect diminishing momentum.

4. Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values — apply a global downward shift of 1–2% to the entire 30d forecast to correct for systematic overconfidence.

5. Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–15 day window — if the 30d history shows a clear downward trend, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for the next 10–15 days to reflect expected correction.

6. Model overreacts to recent volatility — if the last 5 days show high volatility or sharp moves, reduce forecast sensitivity by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
